TASK ID: clique-to-sat

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Clique to SAT. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Clique and TARGET is SAT. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

TARGET = Sat
SAT (CNF satisfiability).

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[literal, ...], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * A clause is a list of any number of literals, including none.
    Literals may repeat, and a clause may contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes). An empty
clause [] can never be satisfied, so any formula containing one is no.

WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-cg3fmxmm

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

We need to know format: Instance of Clique: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}. Need to produce SAT instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[literal,...], ...]}. Reduction: classic: For each position i in the clique (1..k) we need a variable x_{i,v} meaning vertex v is the i-th vertex in the clique. Variables: i from 1..k, v from 0..n-1. total m = k * n. Represent variable index = i * n + v + 1 maybe. Use 1-indexed.

Constraints:

1) Each position i must be assigned at least one vertex: clause (x_{i,0} ∨ x_{i,1} ∨ ... ∨ x_{i,n-1}).

2) No vertex appears in two positions: for each v, for each i<j, clause (¬x_{i,v} ∨ ¬x_{j,v}).

3) For each pair of positions i<j, the vertices assigned must be adjacent: for each non-edge (u,v) (including u=v? not needed) we add clause (¬x_{i,u} ∨ ¬x_{j,v}) and (¬x_{i,v} ∨ ¬x_{j,u})? Actually ensure that if vertices u and v are not connected, they cannot both be selected. So for each pair i<j and each unordered pair (u,v) that is NOT an edge, add clause (¬x_{i,u} ∨ ¬x_{j,v}) and (¬x_{i,v} ∨ ¬x_{j,u})? Since positions are ordered, need both combos. Simpler: for each i<j, for each pair u,v (including u=v?), if edge missing, add clause (¬x_{i,u} ∨ ¬x_{j,v}). That covers both orderings because i<j fixed. Need also ensure u=v case? That is covered by constraint 2 (no same vertex in two positions). So we only need consider u != v non-edges.

Edge cases: k <=0 always yes. So we can output trivial SAT instance that is always satisfiable, e.g., no clauses (empty formula) which is yes. For k=1 always yes if n>=1. We can also output same trivial. For k>n always no, need produce unsatisfiable SAT instance, e.g., a single empty clause [].

Implementation: reduce(instance) returns dict {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [...]}. Should handle edge cases.

We also need to ensure polynomial time; fine.
